headlines.title: Person dies after multi-vehicle crash on Hwy. 101 in San Jose
headlines.description: A person died following a multi-vehicle crash that prompted a partial closure of Highway 101 on Saturday morning in San Jose, the California Highway Patrol said. CHP said the crash occurred around 5:30 a.m., north of the Tully Road off-ramp. Authorities said initial reports indicated the incident involved one vehicle, but it was later determined multiple vehicles were involved. One person died in the crash, according to CHP. Authorities were also advised of a possible ejection and a trapped occupant, adding many vehicles sustained major damage. The crash prompted the closure of all southbound lanes on Highway 101. The lanes reopened around 9 a.m.

headlines.title: Valkyries sweep Aces to clinch first-ever WNBA Finals berth, will face Dream
headlines.description: In just Year 2 of the franchise’s existence, the Golden State Valkyries are headed to the WNBA Finals. After winning Games 1 and 2 at home, the Valkyries defeated the Las Vegas Aces 87-77 in overtime on Friday at Michelob ULTRA Arena to complete a three-game sweep in the semifinals. Kayla Thornton led the way with 18 points and nine rebounds, while Kiah Stokes tallied 11 points, 10 rebounds and three blocks in a thrilling victory to clinch their spot in the WNBA Finals. Next, Golden State will take on the Atlanta Dream, who completed a three-game sweep of their own on Friday to take down the New York Liberty in the other semifinals matchup. The Valkyries won all three regular-season matchups against the Dream, with each game taking place within a two-week span between June 24 and July 4. Game 1 of the WNBA Finals, a best-of-seven series, will tip off on Saturday, Oct. 17 at 12:30 p.m. PT at “Ballhalla,” as the Valkyries have dubbed their home floor at Chase Center. Golden State owns home-court advantage for the series thanks to its higher seed; Games 1, 2, 5 and 7 — the latter two only if necessary — will be held at Chase Center. Despite trailing by nine points at halftime and as much as 11 early in the second half, the Valkyries went on a 17-0 run in the third quarter to claim their first lead of the night over the Aces. The Aces wouldn’t go down easy at home, though, re-taking a six-point advantage in the final three minutes. Three-time reigning WNBA MVP A’ja Wilson wasn’t at her best on Friday, but she still led all scorers with 21 points to go with 10 rebounds. But the Valkyries battled back again, responding with an 8-0 run that helped eventually force overtime. In the extra period, Golden State’s top-ranked defense — along with their leading scorer Gabby Williams — took control. Williams scored eight of her 16 points in overtime, and the Valkyries outscored the Aces 16-6 in the frame. In 2025, the Valkyries made the WNBA playoffs in their inaugural season, losing in the first round to the Minnesota Lynx. A year later, Golden State is four wins away from bringing home a title — and quickly satisfying owner Joe Lacob’s confident declaration that the team would win a championship within its first five seasons. headlines.title: Juveniles identified as suspects in hate crime investigation in San Anselmo
headlines.description: Two juveniles were identified as the suspects involved in a hate crime investigation at an elementary school in San Anselmo, authorities said on Saturday. Central Marin police said two juveniles, ages 12 and 13, were identified as the suspects in the investigation into the antisemitic graffiti discovered at Brookside Elementary School on Oct. 3. The school removed the graffiti after it was reported to the police, according to authorities. Officials believe the incident happened at the end of the school day on Friday, around 8:30 p.m.

headlines.title: Large crowds enjoy Fleet Week events in San Francisco
headlines.description: The Parade of Ships and highly-anticipated Fleet Week Air Show kicked off an expected big weekend of events in San Francisco. While some people plan on waking up early to get a good spot on Marina Green, a special performance from First Marine Division Brass Band took place in Chinatown. “The audience was electric, the people of San Francisco, they’re just really about Fleet Week,” First Marine Division Brass Band Staff Sergeant David Linnenkamp said. Despite low clouds impacting visibility, large crowds gathered Friday in the city to view Fleet Week’s main events. From the parade of ships to the Blue Angeles, to the band performances, everyone seemed to be enjoying all that Fleet Week has to offer. The weekend is expected to draw additional big crowds as the main events continue in San Francisco. Visit our Fleet Week guide for more information and a schedule of weekend events. San Francisco Sep 21 San Francisco Oct 8 San Francisco 24 hours ago

headlines.title: Doja Cat concert rescheduled following Valkyries' advancement to WNBA Finals
headlines.description: Doja Cat’s concert at Chase Center in San Francisco has been rescheduled following the Valkyries’ advancement to the WNBA Finals on Friday, officials announced. Senior Manager of Venue Communications at Golden State Maria Bell said the concert, originally scheduled for Oct. 19, will now take place on Oct. 25. She said all tickets will remain valid for the new date, and more information will be emailed to ticket holders when available. The announcement came after the Valkyries beat Las Vegas Aces 87-77 on Friday, advancing to the WNBA Finals. Now, according to officials, the Valkyries will host Game 1 on Oct. 17 and Game 2 on Oct 19 at Chase Center.

headlines.title: Pro-Palestinian protesters gather outside FedEx facility in Oakland
headlines.description: Hundreds of pro-Palestinian protesters gathered outside a FedEx facility in Oakland on Friday, alleging the company ships parts for F-35 fighter jets that Israel has used in attacks in the Gaza Strip. The protest began Friday morning outside the large FedEx facility on Edes Avenue, not far from Interstate 880. Hundreds of people, including faith leaders, union workers, students and others, participated in the demonstration. The protest comes during the week marking the third anniversary of the Hamas attack on Israel. Israel retaliated by bombing the Gaza Strip, where Hamas is located. Protesters say an F-35 was used in an attack on a refugee camp in Gaza where as many as 120 people were killed. They accuse Israel of genocide and allege FedEx is complicit because the company ships F-35 parts to Israel. Lawsuits have been filed against FedEx in Belgium and France alleging the shipments of F-35 parts to Israel are illegal. NBC Bay Area’s Bob Redell has the full report in the video above.

headlines.title: Bay Area immigrant rights groups prepare amid concerns about increased ICE raids
headlines.description: Bay Area immigrant rights groups are bracing for more ICE raids following published reports suggesting the Trump administration is ramping up its immigration crackdown in California ahead of the November election. The Washington Examine, citing unnamed sources, said ICE launched an enforcement initiative called “Operation Safe California,” and reportedly have been told to arrest any undocumented immigrant. This follows another recent report saying ICE agents were instructed to step up arrest goals from 2,000 a day to 3,000. The Department of Homeland Security and ICE have neither confirmed nor denied there is a special crackdown targeting California. They acknowledged there are arrests goals, but no arrest quotas. In response to the reports, Governor Gavin Newsom wrote on X, “This is exactly what I warned would happen last year. Trump is using mass deportations to TERRORIZE diverse communities out of legally voting — ordering his secret police to ‘go after everybody.’ Donald, your campaign of fear will FAIL. The American people will NOT be intimidated!” The Rapid Response Network in Santa Clara County agreed. “‘Our message to [the] community is ‘Power not panic.’ Stay informed, stay prepared and there are resources available like the ‘Rapid Response Network Hotline’ and ‘Know Your Rights Information’,” Jeremy Barousse with the SCC Rapid Response Network said. The UFW recently published 60 arrests in the Central Valley in one day. The immigrant support group SIREN says the Bay Area has not seen that kind of activity. “That doesn’t mean you can’t be prepared though. Reach out to the Rapid Response Network to get red cards, go through your trainings and make sure to remind yourself what your rights are so that you know not to answer their questions. Do not put yourself at risk if ICE agents approach you,” SIREN Executive Director Huy Tran said. The Lawyers’ Committee for Civil Rights of the San Francisco Bay Area echoed those sentiments but warned an ICE surge can be unpredictable. “When you scale up like this, especially given the history of this agency and the way that it has been very indiscriminate and very, very sloppy in its execution of its arrest priorities, it’s inevitably going to get things wrong and deprive people of their constitutional and civil rights ripped away. We’re anticipating that,” Jacob Gonzalez with Lawyers’ Committee for Civil Rights said. This story uses functionality that may not work in our app. Click here to open the story in your web browser.

headlines.title: Uniqlo opens new flagship store in downtown San Francisco
headlines.description: Uniqlo opened a flagship store on Market Street in San Francisco on Friday, filing a long-vacant storefront. The grand opening had people lining up in a part of the city that people have been leaving in the past few years. The new store will occupy a space of 20,000 square feet on Market Street, and it’s a little piece of Japan. Some people were looking to get in and shop, while others looked forward to the local collaborations. The brand’s former location closed in 2021, during the pandemic. It was one of a series of retailers who left the once vibrant shopping corridor. Downtown and Union Square storefronts still have visible vacancies, but signs are increasingly pointing to a turnaround. “It’s really lovely to see things are kind of popping off downtown again, because for a while downtown was a bit of a ghost town, so it’s really nice to see kind of new life back in the city,” Norway resident Aaron Fowler said. Marisa Rodriguez with The Union Square Alliance agrees. “One of the most busy intersections actually here in San Francisco is saying ‘Let’ go, let’s go, San Francisco, we’re open for business, let’s go Union Square. We are here, we are showing we are making our mark ’,” she said. “And short after we are going to start to see openings from a lot more businesses so stay tuned.” The Alliance says it’s just the latest in a series of big wins for one of San Francisco’s most important locations. “We have the Nintendo store, we have Bape, Sherryl MacMullen if you are into really awesome curated fashion, she is on Maiden Lane. We’re starting to see a resurgence of Maiden Lane as well, cafés like Painted Leopard,” Rodriguez said. The new store is expected to create nearly 100 jobs.

headlines.title: Hurricane Isaias could push California gas prices higher
headlines.description: Hurricane Isaias is raising concerns about what its path through the Gulf could mean for gas prices in California. The Category 2 storm has winds in excess of 105 mph, and its predicted path includes some of America’s most important offshore oil rigs and refineries. Some are warning that as oil rigs go offline, prices at the pump could rise. The exact impact of Hurricane Isaias is still unknown, but any disruption to oil production could cause gas prices in the Bay Area to go up, AAA said. In San Jose, Jose Bracamontes was filling up gas containers for his family’s taco truck, Las Delicias de Toñita. “Filling up gas right now for my parents’ taco truck downtown San Jose, Las Delicias de Toñita,” Bracamontes said. The three containers cost about $95 to fill, not including the propane the family also needs. Fuel costs are eating into the family’s profits. “Yeah, it’s expensive. Everything is getting expensive. The whole economy,” Bracamontes said. Landscaper Jimmy Lozano is also paying to fill up his tools and his truck. He said profits are down. Attention is now on what Hurricane Isaias could do to Gulf oil rigs and refineries. NBC News reports Chevron and Shell have begun shutting down some oil production sites. “If there’s any impact to global oil supply anywhere, it will have an impact on prices at the pump,” said Doug Johnson of AAA of Northern California. Johnson said the majority of the domestic oil inventory is also in the Gulf. “If the power is down for a couple days, it’s not a big deal,” Johnson said. “It’s if they’re down for weeks at a time that will really have an impact.” Consumers like Lozano say first a war and now a hurricane could further impact drivers and their wallets.

headlines.title: ‘$100M' tiny home bros face big 35-count felony complaint, conspiracy accusation
headlines.description: They promised to build tiny homes and help families weather the housing crisis, but prosecutors say some California builders instead diverted hundreds of thousands of dollars of customers’ money. The Sacramento County District Attorney’s office filed a 35-count criminal complaint against Austin and Colton Paulhus, the brothers who co-founded Anchored Tiny Homes. “I cried. But it was a good cry,” said San Leandro resident Katie Lucas, a former Anchored Tiny Homes customer. Online, Colton Paulhus boasted that his Sacramento-area company was putting ADU’s in tons of Northern California backyards and raking in serious revenue in 2023. “I can tell you right now a $100 million business,” he said at one point on his defunct podcast. But now, the Sacramento District Attorney alleges the Paulhus brothers conspired and repeatedly violated state law when they “billed customers and received payment of approximately $1,046,433… despite performing no work and supplying no materials.” Bay Area customers like Lucas came forward in 2024 to tell NBC Bay Area that Anchored Tiny Homes had abandoned their projects after taking tens of thousands of dollars up front. Soon, the business failed and the state revoked its license – forcing many families who’d prepaid Anchored Tony Homes to find a new contractor and pay for some work a second time. Lucas says she’s been waiting for criminal charges. “It’s a relief to know that something is happening. [And] that somebody’s going to be held accountable for what they’ve done,” she said. On page after page of the “Felony Complaint,” the district attorney alleges Austin and Colton Paulhus “did wrongfully divert” money that more than 30 customers had paid them to build an ADU. Count 21 involves Alan Miller in Oakland. “We’re all holding the bag,” Miller said in 2024. When NBC Bay Area visited his abandoned, half-built ADU, he said his family was out $80,000. “For us, it’s just catastrophic,” he said in 2024. “They haven’t told us where our money went.” The complaint says the Paulhus brothers took more than $653,000 from company accounts “for expenses and activity unrelated to company projects.” However, the complaint does not lay out a money trail. Colton Paulhus has said his customers’ money is gone. Currently, he and Austin Paulhus are seeking bankruptcy protection in federal court. Lucas is eager to see what evidence the DA presents in state court. “I’m hoping they are somehow able to uncover where all that money is,” she said. We asked the Sacramento District Attorney’s office for an interview. A rep said, “We do not discuss pending cases.” We also reached out to attorneys for the Paulhus brothers, but did not receive a statement. Back when Anchored Tiny Homes closed its offices, Colton Paulhus sent me a text message that said, “It was a failed business and I hate that it happened.” Lucas winced. “He’s right, it is a business that failed. But it was never going to succeed because of how they ran it.” The Paulhus brothers’ case is on the docket in Sacramento Superior Court next week. NBC Bay Area plans to be in the courtroom. A reminder for you: State law is clear, the maximum a contractor can take from you up front is $1,000.

headlines.title: PG&E warns of possible power shutoffs in parts of Bay Area
headlines.description: Hundreds of Bay Area residents were preparing Friday for the possibility of a PG&E power shutoff due to hot, dry and gusty weather. The potential Public Safety Power Shutoffs would primarily impact a rural area south of the Altamont Pass that includes part of Livermore and unincorporated Alameda County. PG&E has warned 386 customers in that area that they could lose electricity starting Friday afternoon and may not have power restored until noon Sunday. A handful of customers in rural Napa County could also lose power. About 13 counties across California are facing similar warnings. PG&E could shut off power because the weather is expected to be dry, gusty and unseasonably warm. Temperatures in Livermore are expected to climb above 80 degrees. The utility wants to prevent energized power lines from moving in the wind and potentially sparking a wildfire, as has happened in the past. In the Bay Area, only about 400 customers in rural parts of Alameda and Napa counties are expected to potentially be impacted by the Public Safety Power Shutoffs.

headlines.title: Monterey County investigators believe teen mother of deceased ‘Baby Angelita' may have run over the infant
headlines.description: A newborn infant found deceased in Monterey County over two months ago may have been run over by a vehicle being driven by the baby’s 14-year-old mother, county and federal law enforcement said Thursday at a press conference. An infant dubbed “Baby Angelita” was found deceased on Aug. 1 and detectives determined that the child’s 14-year-old mother had been impregnated by her own father, Sergio Galvez Perez. An Amber Alert went out for both of them on Sept. 6 and the Monterey County Sheriff’s Office said Sunday that the pair were located by authorities in Mexico. On Thursday, Sheriff Tina Nieto, the FBI and other law enforcement shed more light on the case that has brought criticism to the Sheriff’s Office and widespread concern about the 14-year-old’s well-being. Thursday was the first time officials revealed that they believe the girl delivered the baby next to a strawberry field in an unincorporated part of the county where she was a laborer and then may have run it over with her vehicle. Evidence at the scene allegedly pointed to the infant being run over by a car, including evidence showing that it was the right front wheel of the sedan, according to Detective Richard Geng with the Sheriff’s Office. “Several feet from Baby Angelita was what appeared to be a large blood stain, which led detectives to believe that Baby Angelita was moved from where she was born to a location under a vehicle that ended up running her over,” Geng said. The vehicle was caught on license plate readers arriving at and leaving the worksite that day and was connected to the 14-year-old’s parents. Investigators believe the girl hid her pregnancy from her mother and that her father was not in the area on the day of the infant’s death. Later that day, law enforcement went to the Salinas home of Galvez Perez and the girl’s mother, Ofelia Garcia Ortega. The girl was found hiding under a pile of clothing and all three were taken to the station for questioning. Initially, the girl told investigators that she had been impregnated by another juvenile, but it was later determined that it had been her father. She was taken to the hospital for post-childbirth care, but her father removed her on Aug. 4 and the two went to Mexico, the Sheriff’s Office said. The case garnered a lot of attention after Nieto initially announced that there was probable cause to arrest the teen for murder. The Sheriff’s Office also initially said the case did not meet the right criteria for an Amber Alert to be issued. Pushback from county Supervisor Wendy Root Askew and the community led the District Attorney’s Office to release a statement that it hadn’t yet charged the girl with anything. Prosecutors have, however, filed charges against Galvez Perez “for the heinous crime of sexually assaulting his own child.” Law enforcement at the press conference Thursday said they have no evidence tying Galvez Perez to the death of the infant and said he was in the Bay Area at the time. Both Galvez Perez and the girl remain in Mexico, though Monterey County authorities are working on extraditing him. They did not comment on whether the 14-year-old girl would be extradited or charged. The girl’s mother was arrested this week in Salinas on suspicion of displaying or possessing a forged identification card, permitting a child to suffer or be endangered, and contributing to the delinquency of a minor.
headlines.source: Katy St. Clair | Bay City News
